The area is much cooler than the coast, so it creates a memorable contrast before the route descends toward the Jungmun and Seogwipo coastline.

/itinerary_variants/1/stops/1/descriptio.source_en: **⟦G0⟧ (한라산 1100고지 습지)** is a high-elevation alpine wetland system on the Hallasan plateau, located **at exactly 1,100 m above sea level** along **Route 1100 — the highest national highway in Korea** linking Jeju City to Seogwipo Jungmun. The site is a **Ramsar Wetland of International Importance (Site No. 1893, designated 12 October 2009)**, falling within the **Hallasan UNESCO World Heritage Site (2007)**, **Jeju Island UNESCO Biosphere Reserve (2002)**, and **Hallasan National Park (1970)** — making this one of the few sites globally with **four overlapping international/national designations**. The wetland comprises **16+ discontinuous freshwater marshes and pools** spread across a low-gradient plateau section that captures and retains rainwater, forming **small permanent lakes and peat bogs** that support diverse floristic assemblages with significant Jeju endemism. Recorded biodiversity includes **3 threatened bird species and 1 threatened plant species within Korea**, plus mammal, reptile, and insect species endemic to Jeju Island. The site received **900,000 visitors in 2008** (Mt Halla Visitor Centre data). Visitor experience: a **1-km wooden boardwalk loop** with observation decks, interpretive signage, and a small natural-history exhibit at the trailhead. **Autumn foliage (October–November)** and **winter snow scenes (December–February)** are the most photographed seasons; **spring + summer** offer wetland flora and endemic species visibility. **FREE admission**; adjacent **1100 Rest Area (1100 휴게소)** provides indoor restrooms + cafe + small souvenir shop. **Cultural and religious importance** to local communities is documented in the Ramsar listing — historical shaman pilgrimages tied to mountain-water spirits.

/itinerary_variants/1/stops/2/whyOnRoute.source_en: **⟦G0⟧ is a compact, high-impact geology stop.** The viewing deck gives guests a clear look at Jeju's columnar basalt cliffs without a long hike, and the site fits naturally after Hallasan 1100 Highland before the route continues toward Seogwipo. The guide may adjust photo time depending on wind, tide, and crowd levels.

/itinerary_variants/1/stops/2/descriptio.source_en: **⟦G0⟧ (대포 주상절리)** is one of Jeju's clearest examples of columnar basalt along the coast. Lava from Hallasan-area volcanic activity cooled and contracted into tightly packed polygonal stone columns, creating the dramatic cliff line now viewed from a safe seaside deck. The columns rise above the waves on the Jungmun coast and are especially photogenic when the sea is active. The visit is short, high-impact, and easier than a long coastal hike, making it a strong stop for mixed-age groups. Walking is mostly on maintained paths and viewing platforms, but wind and sea spray can vary by weather and tide.
